info.name: WideCast.ai
info.description:
WideCast.ai turns plain-text scripts (and soon ideas, audio, existing videos)
into AI-generated short-form videos: scenes + voice + B-roll, ready for
review in the scene editor.

This is the **v0.1.0 pilot surface**. Auth and billing are deferred — see
`widecast/ROADMAP.md` for the full plan.

## Two input flows (`source`) × two completion gates (`output_type`)

### `source` — what kind of input you provide

1. **`source: "text"`** (default) — you provide `script_text` (80-500
   words), used VERBATIM by the narrator. No AI rewriting.
2. **`source: "idea"`** — you provide `idea_text` (5-1000 words, longer
   gets auto-truncated). The server writes a narration from the idea
   (AI), then continues the same scene-sourcing flow as `text`. You
   also pick `language`, `video_length` (short/normal), and
   `research_enabled`.
3. **`source: "blog"`** — you provide `blog_text` (30-3000 words — an
   article to repurpose; longer auto-truncated). Identical pipeline to
   `idea` (same AI script-writer), just a longer input. Same optional
   `language` / `video_length` / `research_enabled`.

`idea` and `blog` are **generative sources**: the server writes the script
first (Phase 1), so they support `output_type: "text"` to stop at the
editable script. Future generative sources (audio, video) follow the
same shape.

### `output_type` — how far down the pipeline to run (pipeline depth)

1. **`output_type: "text"`** — stop after the source→script-text phase.
   Returns a `review_url` (the UI auto-detects the data is narration-only
   and opens the Script Editor). **Only valid for generative sources**
   (`source != "text"`) — for `source: "text"` you already supplied the
   script, so `text` output would echo your input (HTTP 400).
2. **`output_type: "scene"`** (default) — stop at "scenes ready for
   review". You get back a `review_url` to inspect / edit before deciding
   to render the final MP4. Optional follow-up: `POST /v1/export_video`.
3. **`output_type: "video"`** — run end-to-end without manual review.
   `result.video_url` populated when the final MP4 is ready. Use this
   when you trust the generated scenes (programmatic / batch use).

The two axes combine — every valid `source` × `output_type` pair works,
except `source: "text"` + `output_type: "text"` (rejected — see above).

## Endpoints

- **POST `/v1/create_video`** — submit `script_text`/`idea_text` + optional
  `output_type`. Returns a `widecast*` id and initial `status: "processing"`.
- **POST `/v1/export_video`** — for `output_type: "scene"` videos that
  reached `scenes_ready_for_review`, kick the final-MP4 renderer.
  Idempotent — calling twice is a no-op.
- **GET `/v1/status/{id}`** — poll until `status` is `completed` (or
  `failed`). The completion gate depends on the video's `output_type`:
    * text  → `stage: "script_ready_for_review"`, `result.review_url` set.
    * scene → `stage: "scenes_ready_for_review"`, `result.review_url` set.
    * video → `stage: "video_rendered"`, `result.video_url` AND
      `result.review_url` set.

Polling cadence: start at 5s, exponential backoff (×1.5) up to 60s. The
SDKs implement this automatically via `video.wait()`.

## Script bounds (LOCKED)

`script_text` is used **verbatim** by the narrator — no rewriting. The
bounds reflect what fits inside a short-form video:

- **Minimum 80 words** (~20s of narration) — anything shorter renders
  a useless clip.
- **Maximum 500 words** (~120s / 2 min of narration) — beyond this,
  render cost and pacing both suffer.

## Field-requirement convention (LOCKED)

Every constraint on every field — validation bounds, enum values,
required-vs-optional, defaults — appears in **four places**, kept in
sync:

1. **OpenAPI spec** — `description`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `enum`,
   `default`. Single source devs read first.
2. **SDK constants + types** — named exports in `widecast` (Python) and
   `@widecast/sdk` (TypeScript), so callers can refer to them
   programmatically without re-typing the literal.
3. **Markdown docs** — `Field reference` table in each endpoint page.
4. **Server enforcement** — rejected requests must surface a LOCKED
   `error.code` (e.g. `script_too_short`, `invalid_output_type`).

The SDK parity test (`test_script_bounds_constants_locked` and
equivalents) imports each SDK constant and asserts the exact numeric
value — changing one surface without the others breaks the test. New
endpoints MUST follow this same pattern.

## Conventions (locked — changing = breaking)

- Snake_case JSON fields
- **ID format**: `widecast<alphanumeric>` (~20 chars). The server's new-script
  detection checks for the literal `"widecast"` substring, so SDKs/clients MUST
  not strip it. Public id == internal `topic_id` (1:1, no mapping).
- API key prefixes: `wc_live_*`
- Object marker: every resource has `"object": "<type>"`
- Status enum: `pending | processing | completed | failed`
  (`pending` ONLY covers the brief race window between create + worker
  writing the topic row; once the row exists, status is `processing` —
  the abroll worker doesn't increment `step` until the end)
- Error envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "param?",
  "doc_url", "request_id" } }`
- Error codes (v0.1.0): `account_expired | credit_exhausted |
  render_failed | unknown_error | scenes_not_ready | export_failed |
  script_too_short | script_too_long | invalid_output_type |
  invalid_source | idea_too_short | missing_idea_text |
  blog_too_short | missing_blog_text |
  missing_video_url | missing_audio_url | missing_media_file |
  unsupported_media_url | media_too_long | file_too_large |
  invalid_language | invalid_video_length | invalid_research_enabled`
- Headers (every response): `X-Request-Id`, `X-RateLimit-*`,
  `X-WideCast-Version`
- Timestamps: ISO 8601 UTC strings (e.g. `2026-05-19T17:30:00Z`)
- Pagination (future): cursor-based — see `ListEnvelope` schema

item.name: Create a video from a plain-text script.

request.description:
Create a video from either a plain-text script (`source: "text"`) or
a short idea description (`source: "idea"`). The server wraps the
same background workers that power the Script Editor + Idea-to-Video
flows in the Gubo UI.

- Returns immediately with `status: "processing"` (HTTP 202). Poll
  `GET /v1/status/{id}` until terminal.
- If `wait_for_render: true`, blocks up to **60 seconds**. If render
  completes within the window, returns `status: "completed"` (HTTP 200).
  Otherwise returns the in-flight state and the client polls.

### source

- `"text"` (default — backward-compat): provide `script_text`
  (80-500 words, used VERBATIM by the narrator). Worker:
  `request_video_script_from_script`.
- `"idea"`: provide `idea_text` (5-1000 words; >1000 auto-truncated)
  plus optional `language` / `video_length` / `research_enabled`.
  Worker chain: `ai_enhance_script` (idea → narration) →
  `request_video_script_from_script` (narration → scenes).

### output_type

- `"scene"` (default): pipeline stops at scenes-ready-for-review.
  `result.review_url` populated on completion. You can then call
  `POST /v1/export_video` to render the final MP4.
- `"video"`: pipeline auto-chains into the renderer once scenes are
  ready. `result.video_url` populated on completion. No manual
  `/v1/export_video` call needed.

### Bounds (LOCKED — see SDK constants)

| Field | When required | Min words | Max words | Over-max behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `script_text` | source=text | 80 (`SCRIPT_MIN_WORDS`) | 500 (`SCRIPT_MAX_WORDS`) | reject `script_too_long` |
| `idea_text` | source=idea | 5 (`IDEA_MIN_WORDS`) | 1000 (`IDEA_MAX_WORDS`) | auto-truncate, surfaced in `details.input_truncated_from` |
| `blog_text` | source=blog | 30 (`BLOG_MIN_WORDS`) | 3000 (`BLOG_MAX_WORDS`) | auto-truncate, surfaced in `details.input_truncated_from` |

SDKs export these as named constants — refer to those instead of
hard-coding the numbers. Word count = whitespace split, works for
English + Vietnamese.

item.name: Kick the final-MP4 renderer for an already-created video.

request.description:
Pairs with `output_type: "scene"` on `/v1/create_video`. After the
scenes-ready callback (or manual review via `review_url`), call this
to enqueue the final render.

Idempotent — calling twice is a no-op. Returns the current
`/v1/status` snapshot.

Preconditions:
- The video must have reached `scenes_ready_for_review` (HTTP 409 with
  `error.code = "scenes_not_ready"` otherwise).

Post-effects:
- The video's effective `output_type` is promoted to `"video"`.
- The completion gate becomes `result.video_url` non-empty.
- The `video.completed` webhook (if `callback_url` is set) re-arms
  and fires when the MP4 is rendered.

item.name: Poll the current state of a video.

request.description:
Universal status endpoint. v0.1.0 supports only the `widecast*` ids
returned by `/v1/create_video`; future flows will reuse the same
endpoint with new id prefixes.

Recommended polling cadence: **5s initial, ×1.5 exponential backoff,
cap at 60s**. The SDKs' `video.wait()` implements this automatically.

When `status == "completed"`, `result.review_url` is the URL where the
user reviews the rendered scenes + audio. `result.script` is the full
rendered video script JSON (with `segments` populated).
